title: Enterprise Contract Auto-Scorer and Legal Queue Thresholds
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Large enterprise contract redlines (MSA/DPA) create inconsistent triage to Legal and Sales. Right now triage relies on manual intake, causing slow turnaround, overloaded legal queue for obvious low-risk concessions, and missed SLA for high-risk indemnity/liability asks. This adds friction to Dedicated/Private sales and biases pricing negotiations.

Goal: Build an automated contract auto-scorer that tags redlines by risk category (Low/Medium/High) and assigns a legal queue threshold. Score should combine clause fingerprints, deviation magnitude, indemnity/limitation changes, and customer tier. Expose adjustable thresholds in the Console and wire scores into routing (auto-approve below threshold, route to Legal above threshold). Surface suggestions to Sales to speed negotiation and inform pricing adjustments.

Scope: Phase 1 (this ticket): design scoring model, define risk signals, create UI threshold controls in Console (read-only for beta customers), and produce an experiment plan to measure throughput, SLA, and pricing impact. Implementation (ENG) and Legal policy encoding will be separate tickets.

Out of scope: Rewriting contract templates, automated signature flows, or changing final approver rules. This ticket focuses on scoring, thresholds, telemetry, and experiment design.
acceptance_criteria: Risk signal taxonomy defined and reviewed by Legal (indemnity, liability cap, escrow, data residency, audit rights, subprocessor clauses, encryption/KMS exceptions).
Scoring algorithm spec document available: inputs, weights, normalization strategy, and fallback when parsing fails.
Console mockups for threshold controls and per-contract score card reviewed by Design and PM.
Experiment plan with metrics, cohorts, and ramp schedule approved by Growth and Legal.
Telemetry schema defined and sample dashboard created showing queue length, mean time to resolution (MTTR), auto-approve rate, false positives/negatives estimates.
Rollout gating criteria agreed (safety checks, manual override path, audit logging requirements).
success_metrics: Reduce legal triage volume for low-risk contracts by >= 35% in first 60 days of experiment.
Maintain or improve SLA for high-risk contract review (95th percentile <= baseline SLA).
Increase Sales negotiation throughput (contracts closed per rep) by 10% in pilot accounts.
Measure and keep false auto-approve rate < 2% for high-severity clauses.
Collect pricing signal: track uplift/discounts applied when auto-scorer flags elevated risk (metric to inform pricing experiments).
implementation_notes: Scoring inputs: clause fingerprint vector (existing PM-51823 work), natural-language deviation magnitude (token-diff heuristic), named clause flags (indemnity, liability cap, jail), customer tier multiplier (Enterprise/Dedicated/Private), prior concession history for account.

Model: start with rule-weighted linear scorer (explainability required); later iterate to a calibrated classifier if needed. Keep deterministic fallback rules for safety-critical signals (e.g., indemnity > $X always routes to legal).
Parsing: reuse Legal intake parser (ENG-41234) and add confidence score; if parsing confidence < 0.6, route to manual review by default.
Auditability: every decision must produce an SSO-linked audit log entry and attach clause excerpts; include link to GitHub PR for any policy change.
UI: Console panel shows score, top contributing signals, recommended action (auto-approve, sales-guidance, route-to-legal), and override button for admins with justification field.
Data retention: keep scoring metadata for 1 year to allow error analysis and model recalibration; align retention with DPA policy and Legal guidance.
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: Finalize policy taxonomy with Legal and map explicit 'always route' rules.
Week 2-4: Implement scorer spec (ENG) behind a feature flag; build Console threshold UI behind admin opt-in.
Week 4-6: Pilot with 3 Enterprise accounts and internal Sales; collect telemetry and manual-review logs.
Week 6-8: Evaluate metrics; tune weights and thresholds; run A/B test for pricing impact on quoted concessions.
Week 8+: Expand rollout progressively if metrics pass gating criteria; provide a playbook for Sales and CSMs on interpreting score cards.
